---
title: "Verification"
---

This page lists the checks that run on every change, the reference results
they compare against, and their tolerances. Running them needs the build
environment described in [Development](development.qmd).

## Routine checks

From the repository root:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
# macOS; use libphit.so on Linux
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -m
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -r 'echo phpversion("phit"), PHP_EOL;'
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/logistic.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/logistic.php
```

cargo test verifies the independent Rust engine. The extension crate disables its
Rust test harness; explicitly building it and running PHP integration tests are
separate required checks for binding changes. For a release/deployment check,
build with --release and run the PHP scripts against target/release instead.
For documentation-only changes, check links, commands and claims against source;
rerun numerical tests when behavior or implementation changes.

## Probability and descriptive APIs

The offline release gate runs `tests/distributions.php`, `tests/descriptive.php`
and `examples/distributions.php`, along with the Rust distribution/descriptive
suites. Distribution checks include 8,618 reference comparisons, 25 independent
mpmath adjudications and 43 documented boundary differences. Descriptive tests
add 145 R quantities, type-7 scalar/batch identities, strict/explicit-drop missing
policies, pairwise alignment, weight definitions and arithmetic overflow errors.
The [distribution record](verifications/distributions.qmd) describes provenance,
reference limitations and operation-specific tolerances. The [utility contract](descriptive.qmd)
documents undefined correlation separately from numerical failure.
`tests/smoothing.php` compares 15,639 density, bandwidth, interpolation, and ECDF
quantities with R at relative `1e-12`.

Refresh PHP error evidence without changing independent expected values:

```sh
PHP=/path/to/matching/php .context/v02/python/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_distributions.py --stored-references
python3 scripts/reference-manifest.py
python3 scripts/distribution-docs.py
```

Reference regeneration with R or 60-digit mpmath is intentional and separate;
see the comparison page. Distribution scalar/batch/Rust/R/SciPy benchmarks and
the seven-model pre-v0.2 preservation comparison run separately from the gate,
with numerical agreement recorded before distribution timings. Seeded [sampling](rng.qmd)
adds 25 independently generated Python/R cases: 2,000 Rust engine/quantile values
and 1,616 PHP transformed references, plus repeatability, prefix, state-isolation,
domain/limit and moment checks. `tests/rng.php` and `examples/rng.php` run in the
release gate. The [readiness assessment](v0.2.qmd) records remaining release steps.

## Posterior-draw kernels

The release gate includes `crates/stats-core/tests/draws.rs` and `tests/draws.php`.
Both consume 25 independent 80-digit Python Decimal cases, including covariance-map
identities, affine round trips and log determinants. Strict validation includes
zero weights, one effective draw and singular covariance, with explicit failures
for map/affine numerical singularity. Provenance, formulas, numerical tolerances,
reproduction commands and limitations are recorded in [draw numerical notes](draw-numerics.qmd).
The [benchmark](benchmarks/draws.qmd) validates complete outputs against R before
recording timings; it runs separately from the offline release gate.

## PHP intercept and offset contracts

`tests/intercept.php` checks all seven PHP fitters with predictors-only inputs
against the same complete design passed with `intercept: false`. Those results
must be identical, including covariance, likelihood, group effects, row accounting,
and diagnostics. Existing fixtures retain their literal matrices and their PHP
runners explicitly opt out of insertion. No-intercept and intercept-only models
are exercised separately; automatic insertion never changes random-design z.

Poisson exposure checks independently calculate the intercept-only weighted MLE,
its standard error, likelihood and fitted counts. They use absolute tolerances
1e-10 for the coefficient/SE and 1e-9 for likelihood/counts. Rescaling exposure
must shift only the intercept and preserve counts. Default-intercept weighted/offset
fits also match stored R fixtures under the existing 1e-7 absolute + 1e-6 relative
tolerance. Missing offsets participate in the same warning/deletion/strict-rejection
contract as other inputs. The offline release gate includes this suite and the
runnable exposure example.

## Reference and tolerances


`tests/fixtures/ols-r.json` contains deterministic results generated by base R
4.6.1 `lm()`, `summary()`, `confint()` and `logLik()`. R is not a runtime or test
dependency. To regenerate: `Rscript tests/generate-fixtures.R`.
The saved simulated housing observations in `docs/data/housing.csv` are shared
by the PHP example, notebooks and one- and two-predictor reference fits.
To regenerate that dataset intentionally, run `Rscript tests/generate-learning-data.R`
first, then regenerate fixtures, the three-way report and both notebook outputs.
The dataset generator specifies its RNG and seed; ordinary rendering and testing
read the saved observations and do not generate fresh random samples.
Rust and PHP tests compare noisy simple, multiple, no-intercept and correlated
full-rank regressions, and include perfect/zero fits. Tolerance is
`1e-9 + 1e-7 * abs(reference)` for each compared quantity. Perfect fits compare
coefficients, predictions, residuals and standard errors, but omit unstable t/p,
R-squared and likelihood comparisons; Rust also compares finite confidence
intervals. Zero-fit conventions are tested directly. R's undefined quantities
are stored as JSON null. Invalid shapes, insufficient observations and rank
failure are tested separately because this implementation rejects cases that R
may handle by dropping aliased coefficients.

## Current coverage and limits

| Case | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Named simulated housing, one and two predictors | R fixtures, Rust/PHP tests and executed three-way comparison |
| Noisy regression with intercept | R simple and multiple fixtures |
| Multiple predictors | R multiple and no-intercept fixtures |
| Uncentered R-squared | R no-intercept fixture |
| Correlated full-rank columns | R correlated fixture |
| Perfect and zero outcomes | R fixtures plus explicit zero-fit assertions |
| Empty, ragged, mismatched or invalid numerical inputs | Rust rejection tests; PHP rejects infinity and malformed data, drops null/NAN by policy |
| Insufficient degrees of freedom and singular designs | Rust and PHP rejection tests |
| Missing data | PHP checks null/NAN deletion, strict rejection, warnings, row alignment, validation before deletion, and rank/df after deletion |
| Predictor units | Rust test rescales one predictor by 1e-12 |
| Large residual df confidence intervals | Rust compares 95% t critical values with R qt() through 999,997 df |
| Large samples and wider models | Separate release benchmark checks up to one million rows and up to 11 coefficients against R/statsmodels |
| Historical Apple Accelerate trial | Archived correctness and benchmark results; experimental implementation removed |
| PHP numeric types and loading | PHP rejects strings, booleans and malformed rows; checks missing policies and warnings; checks the extension loads |

For ordinary fixtures, comparisons include coefficients, covariance, fitted
values, residuals, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, confidence intervals,
RSS, residual variance, sigma, R-squared, adjusted R-squared and likelihood.
Residual degrees of freedom is also checked. This is a small deterministic suite,
not proof of correctness for every floating-point input. CI runs it on
Linux and macOS, and the packaging workflow runs it on Linux x86_64 and aarch64
at PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, including a PHP-FPM request. It does not exercise
extreme scales or every array-key pattern.

## Maintaining evidence

When changing an estimator or inference calculation, add a case that distinguishes
the intended behavior from the old behavior. Compare against R where its
conventions match ours, and test deliberate differences explicitly. Keep fixture
inputs, generator and expected outputs together. Inspect regenerated fixture
diffs; do not simply relax a tolerance to hide a discrepancy. When reporting
verification, identify which Rust/PHP checks ran and which platform was used.

The current absolute-plus-relative tolerance supports near-zero quantities as
well as larger ones. It does not establish relative accuracy for p-values much
smaller than the absolute tolerance. If a change depends on extreme tails, add
focused reference tests and a suitable tolerance for those values.

## Executed three-way evidence

The [OLS verification report](verifications/ols.qmd) and
[verification notebook](notebooks/ols-verification.qmd) estimate the same cases
afresh in R, Python statsmodels and PHP. Python/R are optional development tools;
the ordinary Rust/PHP tests remain independent of them. The
[math notebook](notebooks/ols-math.qmd) exposes each intermediate calculation.
Follow [notebook setup](notebooks/index.qmd) to regenerate the comparison report
and saved notebook outputs. Each future implemented estimator should have a
walkthrough and equivalent-model evidence where reference support exists.

## Scale and performance checks

The [OLS benchmark report](benchmarks/ols.qmd) records release-extension timings,
input loading, whole-process time and peak resident memory against R and statsmodels.
Its standard cases include 1,000, 100,000 and one million observations with three
coefficients, plus 100,000 observations with eleven coefficients (intercept included).
It checks all inference and scalar statistics and ten sampled fitted/residual
values against R; it does not compare every observation-length output on these
large cases. These checks run separately from the small unit/reference suite.

Run `.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py` after building the
release extension with matching PHP headers. Review raw results and numerical
agreement before reporting speed comparisons. Follow the report for timing
boundaries, backend settings, hardware, reproduction and evidence limitations.

## Binary logistic regression

`tests/fixtures/logistic-r.json` stores base R `glm(..., family=binomial())`
results for simulated students, one predictor, multiple predictors, no intercept,
intercept only, highly correlated full-rank columns, and imbalanced outcomes.
Regenerate intentionally with `Rscript tests/generate-logistic-fixtures.R`;
this also regenerates the saved teaching observations in `docs/data/learning.csv`.
Wald intervals use `confint.default()`, since glm's ordinary `confint()` uses
profile likelihood. Reference fitting uses epsilon 1e-14 to stabilize final
information/covariance agreement.

Rust and PHP tests compare all statistical fields and full observation vectors
with tolerance 1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference). Rejection cases include malformed
inputs, nonbinary outcomes, one retained class, rank deficiency, complete and
quasi separation. Rust tests cover extreme logits and iteration exhaustion.
PHP tests cover listwise deletion, warnings, row accounting, strict missingness
and invalid values before deletion. Three-way verification also checks a sample
with missing rows. These tests do not establish exhaustive separation detection.

```sh
PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php .context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_logistic.py
PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php .context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model logistic
```

See the [verification record](verifications/logistic.qmd),
[executed comparison](notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd) and
[release benchmark](benchmarks/logistic.qmd).

## Probit and Poisson

`tests/fixtures/probit-r.json` and `poisson-r.json` are generated with base R glm,
normal Wald inference and tolerance epsilon 1e-16. Regenerate intentionally with
`Rscript tests/generate-probit-poisson-fixtures.R`; this also writes both shared
teaching samples. Six fixtures per method cover named simulations, one predictor,
multiple predictors, no intercept, intercept only, correlated columns and
imbalanced/sparse outcomes. Three-way scripts add two missing rows and compare
all fields/full observation vectors at 1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference).

Probit comparisons use expected-information covariance in both reference libraries.
Rust tests include underflowing normal log tails, failed convergence and separation.
Poisson tests cover integer validation, zero counts, precision of near-zero deviance,
failed convergence and selected boundary designs. PHP tests check missing warnings,
strict policies, invalid outcomes before deletion, row alignment and convergence
metadata. Existing OLS/logistic tests continue to cover shared binding conversion.

```sh
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/probit.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/poisson.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_probit.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_poisson.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model probit
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model poisson
```

See the [probit comparison](notebooks/probit-verification.qmd),
[Poisson comparison](notebooks/poisson-verification.qmd) and their benchmark pages.
These cases establish tested behavior, not exhaustive separation/boundary detection
or coverage of Linux/PHP-FPM deployment.

## Gaussian random-intercept ML

`tests/fixtures/lmm-r.json` stores six lme4 ML fits: the simulated schools,
one predictor, no intercept, intercept only, an additional singleton group and
an exact zero-between-group-variance boundary. The generator
`Rscript tests/generate-lmm-fixtures.R` intentionally refreshes both fixtures
and `docs/data/schools.csv`. lme4 is a development dependency, never a runtime
requirement. R uses REML=FALSE with bobyqa rhoend=1e-10.

Rust/PHP comparisons cover fixed coefficients, plug-in GLS covariance and Wald
inference, population/conditional fitted values, both residual definitions,
shrunken group effects, variance components, ICC, marginal likelihood and AIC.
Tolerance is 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference), reflecting independently optimized
variance components. A balanced intercept-only case also has independently
known ML variance and shrinkage results. Tests reject invalid/unidentifiable
samples and positive-residual-variance failures, and verify units/row order,
exact boundary behavior, typed group IDs and listwise deletion across x/y/groups.

The [three-way comparison](notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd) uses statsmodels
MixedLM ML estimates with the declared GLS covariance convention. Its exact
zero-variance case uses a separately labeled NumPy OLS-limit check, since a
statsmodels mixed optimizer is not a reliable exact-boundary reference.
It also tests a sample with missing values in all three inputs. The stored report
records the Python backend, warnings and covariance convention for each case.

```sh
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/lmm.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model lmm
```

The finite profile search is not an exhaustive global-optimization proof.
The original fast call remains one random intercept with Gaussian ML. The expanded general fitter now has separate REML/random-slope/multiple-term tests; finite-sample mixed-model inference adjustments remain open.


## Published Gaussian mixed-model data

The [published-data comparison](notebooks/lmm-public-verification.qmd) checks
sleepstudy (180 observations), Orthodont (108), Machines (54) and Hsb82 (7,185)
against R lme4, R nlme and Python statsmodels. Both R packages have saved expected
outputs in `tests/fixtures/lmm-public-r.json`, checked by Rust and PHP without
runtime R/Python dependencies. The live comparison checks full output vectors,
all inference, variance components, likelihood and exact group/sample metadata.
CSV snapshots, original studies, export versions, checksums and explicit matrix
construction are documented in [data provenance](data/lmm/index.qmd).

Published near-zero observation-level differences use a documented 1e-6 absolute
outcome-unit tolerance plus 1e-6 relative. Other fields use 1e-7 absolute plus
1e-6 relative; likelihood/AIC use 1e-7 absolute plus 1e-10 relative. A separate
native-versus-statsmodels check uses the stricter original uniform tolerance.
The notebook includes independent profile-score checks and recorded reference
optimizer rounding, rather than hiding disagreements or changing model conventions.
Run `docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py --public` in the pinned Python environment.

## Expanded R compatibility

[The executed audit](notebooks/r-compatibility.qmd) verifies 12 weighted/offset
fixed-estimator cases and 15 general Gaussian mixed cases. Both native BOBYQA
and Nelder–Mead are compared against actual lme4 bobyqa, Nelder_Mead, nlminbwrap
and nloptwrap reference fits, with saved controls, convergence codes and warnings.
The published sleepstudy random-slope model has ML/REML statsmodels checks too.
The [coverage ledger](r-compatibility.qmd) documents quantity-specific tolerances,
backend differences and unsupported features. New fixture tests need no R;
`compare_r_compatibility.py` adds actual PHP and live statsmodels verification.

## Binomial logit with one random intercept

`tests/fixtures/logistic-mixed-r.json` stores seven datasets at four integration
settings (Laplace, 9, 25, 61 nodes), including published cbpp data and difficult
rare-event/large-variation cases. Rust checks full output against lme4 and tests
normal quadrature moments/tiny tail weights, the ordinary-GLM zero-variance
reduction, predictor units, count canonicalization/limits and failure controls.
PHP integration checks the actual binding, typed labels, complete row alignment,
original-input validation, warnings and strict missingness.

[The executed verification notebook](notebooks/logistic-mixed-verification.qmd)
adds independent SciPy root finding, matched-approximation likelihood evaluation
and QUADPACK integration. It distinguishes R agreement from approximation accuracy
and retains lme4's raw likelihood convention plus the disclosed grouped-binomial
normalization correction. The full Python mixed-model reference is SciPy;
statsmodels' Bayesian binomial mixed estimator has a different objective.

See the [v0.1 stabilization assessment](v0.1.qmd) for the offline `scripts/check` gate,
IDE stubs, structured diagnostics, stress fixtures, provenance manifest,
performance preservation and remaining release/deployment gates.
